rationale: Evidence: iteration 3 (base_speed 1.5, kd 0.5) is the best raced design at 176.2, up from 170.5 at kd 0.4. Oval finishes rose to 3 of 20 and mean oval progress rose to 0.69. Line losses are still about 1.0 per run on the s-bend and 1.05 on the slalom, and every s-bend and slalom run still ends off_track. Lowering speed to 1.3 (iteration 2) made losses worse, so speed is not the lever. The kd steps have been the only changes that helped (kd 0.2 to 0.4 gave +101, kd 0.4 to 0.5 gave +6). The gain per step is shrinking, and steering_oscillation on the oval has risen to about 0.30. Change: kd 0.5 to 0.55, a small single-variable step. base_speed 1.5, kp 4.0, ki 0.2, the geometry and line_loss last_direction are all held, so any change is attributable to kd. Expected result: a small further gain in score (about 176 to 185), with line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom at or slightly below 1.0 and max_error still near 0.06. Risk: steering_oscillation may rise past about 0.32 and cut the gain, in which case the next step is kd 0.5 again and a sensor-geometry test, not kp. Hypotheses: (a) line losses are caused by under-damped response into the sharpest bend, so kd keeps helping with diminishing returns; (b) the remaining losses come from the narrow sensor span (x = ±0.04 m), which may lose the tape before the steering can respond. Measurements wanted next: line_loss_events and max_error per development track, completion and completion_time on the oval, and steering_oscillation to see whether jitter is growing with kd.
